body: `'timeout'` != `'cookieTimeout'` afaik. Did you try the latter? The first is usually a relative value, the second one an absolute one.

Yeah I tried that one as well. No permutation of using both/either of these seems to work..

```
'Session' => [
    'timeout' => 62,
    'cookieTimeout' => 61
]
```

Edit.. also the docs say that if `cookieTimeout` isn't there it'll use the value of `timeout` for it.
I can take a look, this _did_ work at some point.
What exactly is not working @patrickconroy? CakePHP 3 does not change the cookieLifetime, that is your responsibility.
If the docs are right - then setting Session.timeout doesn't affect Session.cookieTimeout, and neither of those things affects the actual expiration of the session cookie.

The docs are wrong. The values that are accepted are:

``` php
     * - defaults: either 'php', 'database', 'cache' or 'cake' as explained above.
     * - handler: An array containing the handler configuration
     * - ini: A list of php.ini directives to set before the session starts.
     * - timeout: The time in minutes the session should stay active
```

I will submit a PR to fix the docs
Thanks @lorenzo, I'll use the ini for the cookie_lifetime.

issue.title: Improved session docs to clarify cookie lifetime and timeouts
issue.body: Added docs to remove inexistent configuration values and to clarify the confusion brought in https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/issues/5664

body:
Sorry if I'm overlooking something but I have not been able to get an authentication cookie to persist past the session. I've read the session docs, I've looked through the core and read Cake\Network\Session.

Using Redis, my Cache configuration looks like:

```
'Cache' => [
  'session' => [
    'className' => 'Redis',
    'duration' => '+1 days',
    'engine' => 'Redis',
    'port' => 6379,
    'timeout' => 1440,
    'prefix' => 'dev:session:',
    'persistent' => true,
    'server' => '127.0.0.1'
  ],
]
```

My session configuration:

```
'Session' => [
  'defaults' => 'cache',
  'handler' => [
    'config' => 'session'
  ],
  'timeout' => 1440,
  'cookie_lifetime' => 1440
],
```

I've added `cookie_lifetime` only because I cannot get timeout to have any affect. I can't find `cookie_lifetime` used anywhere in cake core either even though it's mentioned in the docs. 

I'm using version `3.0.15` which I just updated from `3.0.12` thinking that might be the cause. Not sure if this is an issue with the Redis cache implementation for sessions, if my ini settings still need to be configured even though I'm using Redis, or if I'm just misunderstanding entirely?

But, no matter what I've tried my CAKEPHP cookie always have an `Expires/Max-Age` value of "session" in Chrome resource panel. In Cake 2 that cookie could persist for days by setting timeout.

I've also tried moving the timeout inside the handler property as well as setting the value directly using the Configure static class. 

Session::renew() explicitly defines the timeout

```
setcookie(
            session_name(),
            '',
            time() - 42000,
            $params['path'],
            $params['domain'],
            $params['secure'],
            $params['httponly']
        );
```
I'll see if I can reproduce locally.

Ahh okay thanks. I wasn't aware that the ini settings would need to be changed even with the session being in the cache. I thought maybe the timeout was handled in there. We opted for changing the settings in php.ini instead of in Cake since we have access to that configuration.

Thanks for you quick response and sorry for my delayed one!
